Create test items

Create a small, isolated item family that proves two supply patterns — purchased components and a Job Shop finished product — and carry it through the engineering, costing, and stock data a quantity-one production order needs, so the finished item can be produced and received into the finished-goods warehouse.

  1. 0Confirm the test design
  2. 1Create two item groups
  3. 2Configure the purchased group
  4. 3Configure the made group
  5. 4Verify site creation control
  6. 5Create the three items
  7. 6Build the job shop bill of material
  8. 7Build the job shop routing
  9. 8Confirm costing data
  10. 9Stock the components
  11. 10Qualify the training case

0 Confirm the test design

Warehousing➔Master Data➔Warehouses➔Warehouses

Nothing yet. Every later phase reads a value recorded here, and the one that bites is the warehouse type: a Shop Floor warehouse cannot be received into as a Normal one can, and a description does not say which it is. In this environment purchase against manufacture is a supply-source decision rather than an item-type one, because physical items are all type Product. Show more

  • Select an approved Normal warehouse; do not rely on description alone

1 Create two item groups

Master Data➔Items➔Item Classification➔Item Groups

Item Defaults is keyed by item type and item group, so the group is the handle every default hangs on. Two groups exist because the two roles need different supply sources, and a group is nothing more than a code, a description and a currency until phase 2 attaches defaults to it.

Step

1.5Save the purchased groupThe purchased group is available for defaults
1.6Repeat 1.1–1.5 for the made group made-supply item group — both dedicated groups are available for defaults

  • Use new dedicated group codes rather than changing an existing group

2 Configure the purchased group

Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Defaults

A default combination records, per package, two separate things: whether default data exists for the subentity, shown by the indicator, and whether a new item should receive it, set by the Create check box. A green indicator with the box cleared gives a new item nothing. The Sites check box decides whether new items get a site row automatically. Show more

What LN is doing. The same mechanism as phase 2 with a different supply source and two more packages. Job Shop names manufacture at a production facility as the default source and creates nothing else, and the Production defaults session only opens when Job Shop by Site is active. A Sales default change offers to propagate to existing items, which for an isolated new group is declined.

4 Verify site creation control

Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Control and Defaults by Site

> Warning > This phase has not been walked for the new groups. Capture the Centrally Managed state and the saved Create controls. Show more

Step
Do this
You should see
4.1Open the row for the site from 0.2, Product, and the purchased group from 1.3The purchased site-control row opens
4.2Read Centrally ManagedThe source of the Create controls is visible
4.3If centrally managed, verify Ordering, Purchase, and Warehousing mirror phase 2 and are disabled locally; if not, select them and saveThe purchased site is marked to create those subentities
4.4Repeat 4.1–4.3 for the made group from 1.6, with Ordering, Production, Warehousing, and SalesThe made site is marked to create those subentities

What LN is doing. The Create controls can be governed at the site instead of the company. When Centrally Managed is selected the site mirrors the company defaults and the controls are disabled here; when it is cleared the site's own controls decide, and an item created before this is checked can arrive with fewer subentities than its group promised, with no message naming the cause.

  • Read Centrally Managed; when selected, correct the governing tcibd0502m000 control instead of the site row

What LN is doing. On save, LN gives the new item the supply source, units and subentities its group's defaults promised and, if the Sites box was set, a site row. The saved site row is where the promise is checked: the supply source and the indicators on it prove phases 2 to 4, which is why nothing inheritable is typed here.

What LN is doing. A bill of material is written against the item, per site, and cannot be used for manufacture until its revision is approved; approval and the two use indicators, for planning and for costing, are three separate actions. The material lines carry the issuing warehouse, and the revision's effective date decides whether a production order's reference date selects it.

  • Confirm Site, Product, BOM Quantity, and Effective Date. Do not clear a proposed required value to make the save pass

  • Only Approved bills of material can be used for manufacture. Run Actions➔Approve Revision on the selected row

  • Another BOM already holds it for this item and site — one per item and site for planning, one per product for costing

What LN is doing. The routing gives the production order operations to report complete; without one there are no estimated production costs and nothing triggers the finished-goods receipt. A reference operation is a template that carries its own times into the operation line, and the routing quantity is what makes those times the times for one pair.

  • Use an existing approved value. Do not create a work center, task, or machine from this walkthrough

  • Every column the screen marks required must be filled — Operation, Reference Operation, and Work Center at minimum

8 Confirm costing data

Common➔Standard Costs➔Master Data➔Item - Costing

A production order's estimate reads each material's standard cost, and a parameter decides whether a missing one stops the calculation or silently lowers it. Purchased items get their standard cost from purchase price data, so the two components will have none until phase 9 buys them in.

Step

8.5For any item whose standard cost is missing or unexpected, open Item Standard Costs ticpr3501m000 for that item and effective dateThe actual and historical standard cost structure is shown, or confirms none exists
8.6If any of the three still has no standard cost, stop and obtain the approved cost route before continuingThe estimate calculation is not left to run against missing material costs

  • Its standard cost is calculated from purchase price priority levels; the item needs purchase price data before it will have one

9 Stock the components

Warehousing➔Inventory 360

A production order can be created and released with no stock, but it cannot be finished, because the material issue has nothing to issue. Buying the components in exercises the Purchase defaults and creates the purchase price history their standard cost is calculated from; the inventory figure at the raw-material warehouse, not the receipt status, is the proof.

This phase creates nothing. It checks the family against what Production order asks for in its phase 0, and hands over.

What LN is doing. Nothing new. This phase checks the family against what the production-order walkthrough's phase 0 asks for and hands the values over. The boundary is here because a fact lives in one file, and the order itself belongs to that walkthrough.

  • Compare the order's reference date with the effective dates from steps 6.7 and 7.7. A revision effective after the reference date is not selected

  • Recheck phase 7 — an approved routing with at least one operation is what phase 5 of the production-order walkthrough reports against

  • Production order

Different cases

  • Create only one purchased material and one Job Shop finished product. This proves the two supply patterns but gives the later BOM only one material class

  • Use this full walkthrough: two purchased inputs and one Job Shop finished product

  • Add a semi-finished level only after the single-level case works; it requires another made-item master, BOM, routing, and costing layer, and a second production order

  • Use another dedicated Product group with Default Supply Source = Purchase; no Job Shop Production defaults are required, and phases 6–7 do not apply

  • Book proportionally more component stock in phase 9 — 2 rods and 1 sleeve per pair. Nothing in the phase structure changes

  • Stop after phase 5. The family exists as master data but cannot be produced; phases 6–10 are what make it runnable

Run order planning

Make one finished item visible to planning, give it a demand it cannot cover from stock, run MRP, and read the result — a planned supply chain covering the shortfall — in the Item Order Plan, in Planned Orders, and in the pegging tree.

  1. 0Make the item visible to planning
  2. 1Create demand
  3. 2Put the demand inside the horizon
  4. 3Run MRP
  5. 4Review the result
  6. 5Read the pegging tree

0 Make the item visible to planning

Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan

> Prerequisite > A finished item with an Approved BOM and routing, components, and stock data — the qualified training case from Create test items. The 2026-08-20 session used BAM-CHOP-PAIR with components BAM-ROD and BAM-SLEEVE.

Step
Do this
You should see
0.1Open Item Order Plan cprrp0520m000The plan selection screen
0.2Search for the finished item finished item — if it appears, planning data exists: go to 0.6. If it does not, the item is invisible to planning: continue
0.3Open Items tcibd0501m000 via Master Data➔Items➔Items and drill into the finished itemItem tcibd0501m100 opens
0.4On the Clusters tab, add a row with the environment's planning cluster planning cluster and site — the observed environment uses NA1 and CSADNA01
0.5Save, then reopen Item Order Plan and search againThe item now appears — an empty plan, but a plan
0.6Repeat 0.2–0.5 for every component in the BOM components given plan data — each appears in its own Item Order Plan

What LN is doing. The planning screens read an item's planning data, and an item that has none is not refused; it is absent, with nothing to explain why. The link is a row for the planning cluster on the item, and MRP plans a BOM component only if the component has planning data of its own, so this phase checks every item in the structure, not just the parent.

  • It has no planning data — no cluster row, no plan. Steps 0.3–0.5. Not an error state; nothing will tell you

1 Create demand

Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench

Planning acts on uncovered demand. A sales order for more than is on hand creates a shortfall, and that shortfall is exactly the quantity MRP should propose, which is what makes the run checkable. Planning sees the demand without the order being approved. Show more

Step
Do this
You should see
1.1In Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000, read the finished item's on-hand at its warehouse finished item on-hand before — the demand must exceed this
1.2Create a sales order for the finished item, following Ship from stock phase 1 steps 1.1–1.11An order exists at Free
1.3Set Ordered Quantity above the on-hand from 1.1, and the Planned Delivery Date no more than a few days out sales order number, ordered quantity, planned delivery date — the observed run booked 5 ea against 1 on hand

  • The item has no row for the order's sales office. Add it on the Sales Offices tab of Item tcibd0501m100, then close and reopen the order session

  • The session was already open when the data changed. Close it and reopen — observed twice on 2026-08-20

2 Put the demand inside the horizon

Planning➔Master Data➔Items➔Items - Planning

The order horizon decides which demand planning sees at all: demand beyond it is not late or flagged, it does not exist to planning. LN turns the number of days you enter into a date by counting workdays on the calendar of the item's warehouse, so the date it shows is the one to trust.

Step
Do this
You should see
2.1Open Items - Planning cprpd1100m000 for the finished item, Horizons tabOrder Horizon as a number of days, with the resulting date beside it
2.2If the delivery date from 1.3 falls beyond the horizon date, raise the Order Horizon days until it falls inside order horizon — record both the days entered and the date displayed
2.3Save, and reopen Item Order Plan cprrp0520m000 for the itemThe Horizons block shows the new Order Horizon date
2.4Find the demand in the gridA Sales Order row with your order number and quantity as Demand

  • The delivery date is beyond the Order Horizon date. Step 2.2 — and remember the date is not today plus your days

3 Run MRP

The run reads every demand inside the horizon, nets it against stock and existing supply, and generates planned orders for the shortfall, multi-level through the BOM when child items are included. With pegging relations updated it also records which demand each planned order exists to serve, which is what phase 5 reads.

Step
Do this
You should see
3.1Open Generate Order Planning (Item) cprrp1220m000 for the finished itemScenario and Plan Item are set
3.2Select Include Child ItemsThe run will also plan the BOM components — multi-level, top-down
3.3Confirm Update Pegging Relations is selected, where the field is openPhase 5 depends on it — see the notes
3.4Run the generationThe run completes; exception messages print or store if selected

  • The component has no planning data of its own. Step 0.6 — MRP skips it silently

  • Check which item you launched the generation on. Running it from a component does not traverse upward — re-run from the top-level (finished) item, per step 3.1

  • It may be correctly absent — planning proposes supply only for what stock does not cover. Read the component's own Item Order Plan and its on-hand before assuming the fix failed. Observed unexplained on 2026-08-25

4 Review the result

One planned order plays two roles: it is supply on the parent's plan and demand on the component's, and the component's own plan has already answered it. Planned quantities equal the raw shortfall only when the item's ordering data imposes no lot-size rule; a minimum or a multiple changes the number before you see it.

Step
Do this
You should see
4.1Reopen the finished item's Item Order PlanThe sales order row now has a companion
4.2Read the planned supply row planned production order number and planned production quantity — a Planned Production Order whose Supply equals ordered quantity minus on-hand
4.3Open the component's Item Order PlanThe same planned production order appears — as Demand
4.4Read the component's planned supply row component planned purchase order and component planned quantity — a Planned Purchase Order covering what stock does not
4.5Open Planned Orders cprrp1100m000 for the cluster and site from 0.4Both planned orders listed, Order Status Planned

  • Order-quantity rules in Items - Ordering tcibd2100m000 round it — "Lot sizing", cpordplanug p. 21

  • If the item is a purchase schedule item, supply transfers straight to Purchase Control and no planned purchase order is created — cprrp1100m000 help

5 Read the pegging tree

The pegging tree walks the relations the run recorded: upstream, what will supply this demand; downstream, what demand caused this order. The tree exists only if pegging relations were generated, which in this environment happens on every run because the option is locked on.

Step
Do this
You should see
5.1In Planned Orders, select the planned production order from 4.5—
5.2Run Pegging - UpstreamOrder Pegging cprrp0740m200 opens as a tree
5.3Read the tree from the topThe sales order, then each level of stock and planned supply beneath it
5.4Check the arithmetic at every level against the BOM and the stock figures pegging arithmetic check — each level's children sum to its requirement

  • Pegging relations were not generated, or the demand lies beyond the Pegging Horizon cprpd0100m000. See the phase 5 Prerequisite

  • Not documented for this release.

  • Adjust order-quantity rules in Items - Ordering tcibd2100m000 and rerun phase 3

Different cases

  • Generate Order Planning cprrp1210m000, Planning➔Order Planning➔Generate Order Planning, runs ranges instead of one item — the production habit. No help is filed for it, so its options are not assumed to match cprrp1220m000's

  • Run a Net Change Planning in the generate session — simulates only from the first net-change date. A value change inside one step, not a phase change

Nothing yet. A production order is built from master data that must already exist, and LN will not say at creation which of it is missing or wrong; it says so at release, at material issue or at completion. This phase reads the finished item, its component, the BOM and routing revisions, the warehouses and the stock before the order asks for them. Show more

3 Release the order

Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders

Release changes the order to Released, the state in which production can start, and at the same moment LN creates two warehousing orders: one to issue the component out of its warehouse and one to receive the finished item into its own. Phase 4 works the first; phase 5 depends on the second.

Material issue turns the estimated quantities into an outbound warehousing order from the raw-material warehouse to the work center, and each issued quantity books a WIP transaction. Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Control➔Report Operations

Reporting the last operation complete records the quantity produced and, depending on a parameter, posts it to inventory silently, not at all, or after asking. The order becomes Production Completed when reported and Completed only when Warehousing finishes the inbound receipt, so the two statuses are a handoff, not a failure. The phase ends with an inventory read because the Manufacturing-side status alone does not prove the stock arrived. Show more

Warehouse transfer

Move a quantity of one item from a source warehouse to a destination warehouse, both in the same logistic company, using a manually created warehousing order — and verify that on-hand at the source dropped and on-hand at the destination rose by the same quantity.Needs · Know the item's stock before you start: Check an item's inventory.

  2. 1Create the transfer order

0 Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type

Warehousing➔Inventory 360

Nothing yet. Reading inventory does not change with the transaction type, only what happens to the order does, and a transfer is proved at both ends, so both starting figures are needed. The expected order type comes from the origin and transaction-type combination in Default Order Types by Origin, and its warehousing procedure is what will decide which later steps LN runs itself. Show more

Do this

0.4Find the row with transaction type Transfer, ship-from Warehouse, and ship-to Warehouse expected warehousing order type; Create Shipment. For different source and destination warehouses, official help states Create Shipment = Always

A manually created warehousing order has no originating package, so the transaction type is set by hand and the order number comes from the Warehousing number group rather than from a sales or purchase order. For a same-company transfer LN copies the outbound and shipment activities and then the inbound and inspection activities onto this one order, so it carries both sides of the move.

Different cases

  • LN generates two warehousing orders instead of one: the ship-from company's order carries the outbound and shipment activities, the ship-to company's carries inbound and inspection. Ship-to Code becomes meaningful. This changes the phase structure (an order-handoff phase is needed) and earns its own walkthrough rather than a bullet here

  • Transfer Order Planning cppat1210m000, reached via Planning➔Plan Transfer➔Transfer Order Planning, generates transfer orders from planned inventory transactions rather than a person entering one by hand. Out of scope for this walkthrough.

  • The order header's Reclassification tab applies to rental and serialized transfers specifically. This variant is outside the scope of the base walkthrough. Source: Infor LN help for Warehousing Order whinh2100m100, Field Information — Reclassification (Rental Product Transfer, Serial Number)

2 Release to warehousing

Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench

Releasing hands the approved lines from Sales to Warehousing: LN creates a warehousing order that carries the sales order's number, and from here the activities of the warehousing procedure, not the sales order, decide what happens next. The release runs from the Actions menu; the Lines ready for panel only counts.

What LN is doing. A planned order is a proposal that no other module can see. Confirming marks it approved, and transferring translates it: a planned production order becomes a production order in Job Shop Control and a planned purchase order becomes a purchase order in Procurement, decided by the item's supply source. A transfer run against unconfirmed orders appears to do nothing.
